'''Nora Berrah''' is an Algerian physicist who studies how light and matter interact. She is a professor at the [[University of Connecticut]], where she previously was chair of the physics department.

Berrah earned a diploma in physics in 1979 from the [[University of Algiers]]. She completed her PhD in 1987 from the [[University of Virginia]]. She worked from [[Argonne National Laboratory]] from 1987 to 1992, and became a professor at [[Western Michigan University]] in 1999. She moved to the University of Connecticut in 2014.{{r|joins|newhead}}

Berrah was elected as a [[fellow]] of the [[American Physical Society]] in 1999.{{r|faps}} In 2014 she won the [[Davisson–Germer Prize in Atomic or Surface Physics]] "for pioneering experiments on the interaction of atoms, molecules, negative ions and clusters with ionizing vacuum ultraviolet and soft x-ray photons".{{r|dgp}} She was elected to the American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) in 2018 and her citation is for "For distinguished contributions to the field of molecular dynamics, particularly for pioneering non-linear science using x-rays free electron lasers and spectroscopy using synchrotron light sources".
She was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2019 and the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amacad.org/news/2019-members-announcement|title=New 2019 Academy Members Announced|publisher=[[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]|date=April 17, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=30 April 2024 |title=National Academy of Sciences Elects Members and International Members |url=https://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2024-nas-election.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240430193331/https://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2024-nas-election.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 30, 2024 |access-date=12 May 2024 |website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref>
